The quote states that NCL diseases have been 'characterized by lysosomal defects leading to the accumulation of undigestible material.' Lysosomal defects are the mechanistic basis of the disease phenotype. Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis is synonymous with NCL and is the subject. Lysosomal defects represent the biological mechanism underlying the disease.

The quoted sentence alone does not fully support the relationship, but the surrounding context establishes it. The abstract states that 'further research on the NCLs suggests that altered protein secretion may also play an important role' and 'Accumulated evidence links seven of the 13 known NCL-related genes to protein secretion, suggesting that altered secretion is a common hallmark of multiple NCL subtypes.' This clearly establishes altered protein secretion as a key mechanism in NCL/neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis. The quoted sentence provides evidence that research findings support this conclusion.
